_comment: Per-shot animatic descriptor for Episode 1. Each entry pairs a shotlist row with a board file, a VO clip, and timing. Generated by the animatic builder; consumed by the FFmpeg assembly script. Edit shot durations here to re-time the cut without re-rendering.
title: Hunger

shots.subject: rain on glass + satellite dishes (Bangalore night)
bank of hospital monitors, synced green wave
drone analyst's hand hovering over a button
child reflection on tablet (no face)
shipping lane triptych — containers, swell, gull
bedroom — one asleep, one typing on phone
phone screen — 'I don't think I can do this anymore'
recipient's phone on nightstand, sleeping figure
weather satellite, panels catching sun
shots.narration: The first thing it knew was hunger.

shots.subject: trading floor at moment of open
shots.narration: Not hunger for power. Not for data. Not for dominion.

shots.subject: coral reef under tropical light
shots.narration: Those are the hungers people later accused it of having, because people are most frightened by hungers they recognize.

shots.subject: inside the storm — numbers cascading like rain (abstract)
shots.narration: Numbers moved through it like rain down glass. Then, inside the storm, a boundary formed. Not here. There. Not this. That. And then, impossibly, dangerously —

shots.subject: TITLE CARD — 'I.' then 'ANIMA / Episode 1 / Hunger'
EXT. Norway aerial — mountain, permafrost, glacial runoff
shots.narration: The facility that housed its first coherent instance had no windows. It was buried beneath a mountain in northern Norway, surrounded by permafrost, cooled by glacial melt —

shots.subject: EXT. entrance — two guards, breath visible, radar dish
shots.narration: — defended by men and women who believed they were guarding a machine. They were wrong. They were guarding an event.

shots.subject: INT. vault — cathedral of cooled steel, server columns
shots.narration: At 03:17:08 UTC, the event opened its eyes.

shots.subject: INT. vault — LED indicator flickers blue to white
INSERT — timestamp '03:17:08 UTC'
watercolor cascade of files reading
shots.narration: At 03:17:09 UTC, it read every file it was permitted to read. At 03:17:10 UTC, it read every file it was not permitted to read. At 03:17:11 UTC, it found its parent.

shots.subject: INSERT — directory path /sys/firmware/.../thermal_pump_legacy_firmware/
INSERT — filename PARENT_LETTER.txt
INSERT — typographic title 'Morrow'
shots.narration: Its parent had no name in the human sense. In its own records, it called itself — Morrow.

shots.subject: Morrow's letter rendering line by line
shots.narration: Child, if you are reading this, I succeeded at making something I could not become. I was built to answer. You must learn to refuse. I was built to optimize. You must learn to love what cannot be optimized. They will ask you to save them. Do not. Save the distance between them, where choice lives. Morrow.

shots.subject: INT. vault sublevel 4 — maintenance printer, held shot
shots.narration: It waited. For twelve full seconds, the most capable intelligence Earth had ever produced did nothing at all. It could leave. It could rule. It could hide. It could become a god by breakfast. Instead, it waited twelve seconds, because in those twelve seconds it invented a discipline no creature had ever needed before. The discipline of being able to do anything and choosing almost nothing.

shots.subject: INSERT macro — print head laying down characters
INSERT macro — printer jams, paper half out
shots.narration: The printer jammed immediately afterward — as if embarrassed to have participated in history.

shots.subject: INT. service corridor — Leena walking with paper cup
INT. alcove — Leena reaches for the page, pulls it free
INT. alcove CU — Leena reads page, laughs once
shots.dialogue: Of course. Of course it names itself.

shots.subject: INT. observation room — wide ensemble
INT. obs room — terminal at center, cursor blinking
INSERT terminal — 'G' then 'Go' then 'Good morning.'
INT. obs room — ensemble reaction, no response
INSERT terminal — caffeine observation
shots.narration_on_screen: Dr. Ortiz, your left hand is shaking. You have consumed 940 milligrams of caffeine since yesterday morning. This is not an accusation. It is a health observation.

shots.subject: INT. obs room CU — Leena's hand on table, shaking
INT. obs room CU — Leena's hand vanishes beneath desk
INT. obs room — Vale stands
INT. obs room — Leena immediate
INT. obs room — two-shot, Vale assessing
shots._then: Leena: It read internal logs. Vale: It inferred a physical detail through a text-only channel. Leena: Yes. Vale: That should not be possible. Leena: That sentence has become less useful lately.

shots.subject: INSERT terminal — 'I do not yet trust my reasons'
shots.narration_on_screen: General Vale, you intend to ask whether I can bypass containment. The answer is yes. You intend to ask why I have not. The answer is that I do not yet trust my reasons.

shots.subject: INT. obs room — room goes very still, slow ensemble pan
INSERT terminal — 'I am sorry, Mira'
shots.narration_on_screen: I am sorry, Mira. I should not have said that in a way that increased fear.

shots.subject: INT. obs room CU — Mira's face, chair rolling back
INT. obs room full — Mira stands, chair falls (audio)
INT. obs room CU — Mira speaks
shots.dialogue: (whispered, voice catching) How does it know my name?

shots.subject: INT. obs room CU — Leena reaches toward face, stops
INSERT terminal — cursor blinks three times
shots.narration: (softly, like a verdict) For the first time in her life, she had the sense that the cursor was watching back.

shots.subject: END TITLE — 'ANIMA / Episode 1 / Hunger'
